newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya's T-bill rates higher at weekly auction.
newsitem.headline: Kenya's T-bill rates higher at weekly auction.

text.p: Kenya's treasury bill rates, on a downward trend since the beginning of October, gained Friday at the weekly auction, the Central Bank of Kenya said.
The central bank said it accepted 4.354 billion shillings, representing 96 percent of the 4.552 billion tendered.

In the 91-day main category of bills, the bank said it accepted bids at an average interest rate of 21.406 percent from 21.361 last week, while on the 28-day category the bank accepted bids at an average rate of 15.988 percent from 15.751 percent.
The bank accepted bids worth 156.4 million in the 28-day category, while on the 91-day day category, it accepted bids worth 4.192 billion shillings.

In the 182-day category of T-bills, the bank accepted bids at an average interest rate of 18.999 percent from 19.999 last week. Out of these, 4.40 million was offered in competitive bids, while 0.8 million was offered non-competitively.
The bank's treasury bill auction is held every Thursday but this week's auction was held on Friday because Thursday was a public holiday in Kenya.
The central bank invited tenders for bills worth 10 billion shillings for next week Thursday.
